description:
Spider Plant (Chlorophytum spp.) is considered non-toxic to cats and is safe for them to be around. However, it contains mild chemical compounds that can have a slightly hallucinogenic effect on felines, similar to catnip but much weaker. This is why some cats are very attracted to spider plants and may chew on them obsessively.

While the plant itself is not poisonous, eating too many leaves can irritate a cat's stomach. This may lead to mild symptoms like vomiting, drooling, or diarrhea. The effects are generally not serious and do not require medical treatment.

Because of the attraction effect, your cat might repeatedly nibble the plant even if it causes them mild stomach upset. If you notice your cat is eating the plant frequently or showing signs of discomfort, it is best to move the plant to a location where they cannot reach it.
name: Spider Plant
safetyNotes: Classified as non-toxic, but contains mild hallucinogenic compounds that may attract cats
Symptoms if eaten excessively: mild GI upset (vomiting, diarrhea), apparent intoxication or unusual behaviour
The mild attraction effect is why some cats repeatedly chew spider plants despite GI upset
Not a medical emergency; limit access if your cat obsessively chews the plant
No veterinary treatment required for typical small-amount nibbling

symptoms.name: Mild nausea or digestive upset (which may include vomiting)
